audit.whatIsWrong: Olaf's W is called 'Vicious Strikes' in four places — spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0], content.late and whys[0] — and it is described as a lifesteal steroid. His W is Tough It Out: bonus attack speed and a SHIELD. Vicious Strikes was the old ability and it has not existed for years.
audit.why: Wrong name and wrong mechanic together. The lifesteal in this matchup comes from Berserker Rage, his passive, and it scales with his MISSING health — so it does not turn on when he presses a button, it turns on when Kassadin chips him. That inverts the advice: a half-finished trade is worse than no trade, because it puts him into the part of his health bar where he heals hardest.
audit.corrected: Tough It Out and Berserker Rage named correctly, with the missing-health scaling stated, in spikes[0].text, wants.foe[0], whys[0], whys[6], content.early, content.late and tradeBad.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ragnarok's condition is absent. Riot's text: he is immune to disables 'for as long as he keeps attacking'. Both layers present it as a flat CC-immunity window to be waited out.
audit.why: It is a condition Kassadin can actually break — his kit is nothing but disengage, and an Olaf with no target to attack stops being unstoppable. 'Wait 100 seconds' and 'take his target away' are very different instructions.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[2].text, wants.foe[1], content.mid, winCon and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow's reset is mentioned as 'the pickup' without either number: a flat 9s cooldown at 1000 range, fully reset when he collects the axe.
audit.why: Denying the axe is the single highest-value thing Kassadin does in the first three levels, and the page asks for it without saying what it is worth. Nine seconds versus zero is the whole reason to body the pickup spot.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into phases[0].why, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, whys[2] and content.early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Reckless Swing's range (325) and resource (health, not mana) never appear, though its true damage does.
audit.why: 325 is barely outside melee, so the true damage the page warns about has a very specific radius — and because it costs him health, spamming it feeds his own Berserker Rage ramp. Both facts change how a disengage is timed.
audit.corrected: Added to phases[1].why, wants.you[2], tradeGood and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating reads 8/10 and both rating lines say 'Hard matchup', while full.diff reads EVEN and the packet records exactly 50% over 12 games.
audit.why: An 8/10 is the grade for a losing lane. This one is level on the data the page itself carries.
audit.corrected: diffRating 8/10 to 5/10 and both rating lines reworded to 'Even matchup', matching diff=EVEN. Olaf's carry threat left at 8.5/10 — his early all-in genuinely is that strong, which is what the 8 was measuring.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] to [6] are the generic Kassadin boilerplate; phases[6].why calls two items 'the monster is awake' on a row the chart sides Olaf.
audit.why: The full layer's late rows and the content layer's late rows say opposite things about who owns the game — content.late opens 'This is your half of the lane' while phases[5] and [6] are both sided Olaf.
audit.corrected: phases[0] through [4] and phases[6] rewritten around Undertow's reset, Reckless Swing's range and Ragnarok's window.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] says 'Force Pulse only charges as spells fly' while content.mid on the same page says 'its cooldown drops every time a spell is cast nearby'. Only the second is current.
audit.why: Force Pulse stopped being charge-gated in V12.23; it is a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown that ability casts within 1800 units shorten by a second each. The kit file still reproduces Riot's pre-rework tooltip, which is why the stale phrasing keeps reappearing — including in phases[2].why here.
audit.corrected: whys[2] and phases[2].why moved to the cooldown model, matching content.mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late instructs the player to 'Q-silence the counterplay', and tradeGood/dosFull/dontsFull repeat 'repeat every six seconds'.
audit.why: Null Sphere has no silence — damage, a channel interrupt and a magic shield — and nothing in Kassadin's kit runs on six seconds.
audit.corrected: Silence replaced with the shield; the cadence replaced with Ragnarok's real 100s clock.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Olaf and you just accept it — your only defensive button is Null Sphere's 1.5s shield, and his Undertow (Q) slow lets him stick while Vicious Strikes (W) sustains him through any trade you try. Don't auto-trade; last-hit from max Q range and bank the CS, because Void Stone's magic reduction does nothing against his physical axes and his Reckless Swing (E) is true damage anyway. The one trap to dodge is the Undertow axe on the ground — standing where it lands lets him grab it to reset the slow, so deny that spot and never walk into a slowed all-in this early.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Olaf and you just accept it — your only defensive button is Null Sphere's shield, and Undertow's slow reaches 1000 to let him stick while Berserker Rage lifesteals harder the lower he gets. Don't auto-trade; last-hit from max Q range and bank the CS, because Void Stone does nothing against physical axes and Reckless Swing is true damage anyway. The one trap to dodge is the axe on the ground: collecting it fully RESETS a flat nine seconds, so body that spot and never walk into a slowed all-in this early.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are where you take over. Nether Blade's mana restore finally lets you farm without going dry, and at 6 Riftwalk changes the math — you can blink over his Undertow (Q) or out of his dive instead of getting slowed and chunked. Trade in short windows: blink in, Force Pulse the cone (its cooldown drops every time a spell is cast nearby), and walk the gap before Reckless Swing (E) connects. The thing to respect is his Ragnarok (R) — it makes him CC-immune and his E true damage ignores your shield, so if he ults onto you, blink away and re-engage once it's burning rather than facetanking the all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are where you take over. Nether Blade's mana restore finally lets you farm without going dry, and at 6 Riftwalk changes the math — you blink over his Undertow (Q) or straight out of his dive instead of getting slowed and chunked. Trade in short windows: blink in, Force Pulse the cone (its cooldown drops every time a spell is cast nearby), and leave before Reckless Swing's 325 range connects. Respect Ragnarok (R): he is immune to disables only for as long as he keeps attacking, so take the target away from him rather than facetank the window.

edits.before: This is your half of the lane. The permanent rule stays the same: respect Ragnarok (R), because the CC-immunity and Reckless Swing (E) true damage still cut through Void Stone and your Q shield, so blink-spam around the ult window rather than sitting in it, and you win the straight 1v1 from two items on.

notes: SECOND STALE ABILITY NAME FOUND IN THIS SLICE: Olaf's W is Tough It Out (attack speed plus a shield). The page calls it 'Vicious Strikes' — the pre-rework name — in four strings, and attributes lifesteal to it. The lifesteal is Berserker Rage, the passive, and it scales with his MISSING health. Together with Mordekaiser's Q being called 'Mace of Spades' on that page, this looks like a shared source of pre-rework ability names rather than two isolated typos; worth a grep across champ-data for other retired names. BLOCKED BY THE LENGTH BAND: content win[] and full phases[] side Olaf at first item AND two-plus items, while content.late opens 'This is your half of the lane' and whys[5]/whys[6] both describe Kassadin winning from two items. 'Olaf' is 4 characters against 'Kassadin' at 8 (+100%) and 'Skill' at 5 (+25%, but wrong) — the correction is out of band, so the last two chart rows need a hand fix. CHAMPION-WIDE, VERIFIED ON THE WIKI: Force Pulse has not been charge-gated since V12.23 — and this page contradicts itself about it, with content.mid using the correct cooldown-reduction wording and whys[2] plus phases[2].why using the retired charge wording. Void Stone is also 10% magic reduction, not the 15% written across the champion (V11.24); it does not appear in this matchup's strings but does in most others. _missing-interactions.json's entry here ('Olaf can cancel your Null Sphere with Ragnarok') is inverted — Null Sphere interrupts channels rather than being one — and was not used.
